relationships.subject: vlPAG GABAergic neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: Our study showed that inhibition of vlPAG GABAergic neurons significantly attenuated the conditioned place aversion (CPA) induced by hindpaw pain pinch or naloxone-precipitated morphine withdrawal.

relationships.subject: pinch pain
relationships.evidence_quote: The IHC and western blotting results showed that AKAP150 expression in the vlPAG increased significantly in both the pinch pain CPA model and morphine withdrawal CPA model

relationships.subject: morphine withdrawal
relationships.evidence_quote: The IHC and western blotting results showed that AKAP150 expression in the vlPAG increased significantly in both the pinch pain CPA model and morphine withdrawal CPA model

relationships.subject: AKAP150
relationships.evidence_quote: Knockdown of AKAP150 in GABAergic neurons effectively reversed the p-TRPV1 upregulation in these two CPA models utilized in our study.

relationships.subject: AKAP150
relationships.evidence_quote: In AKAP150<sup>flox/flox</sup> mice and C57/B6J wild-type mice, cell-type-selective inhibition of AKAP150 in GABAergic neurons in the vlPAG attenuated aversion.

relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: These data suggest that silencing TRPV1 in GABAergic neurons of the vlPAG can attenuate the CPA response induced by pinch pain or morphine withdrawal.

relationships.subject: pinch pain
relationships.evidence_quote: our immunofluorescence and western blotting assays showed that phosphorylated TRPV1 (p-TRPV1) increased significantly in pinch pain CPA model mice

key_findings: Chemogenetic inhibition of vlPAG GABAergic (but not manipulation of glutamatergic) neurons attenuated conditioned place aversion induced by pinch pain or morphine withdrawal.

AKAP150 and phosphorylated TRPV1 were upregulated in vlPAG in both CPA models; knockdown of AKAP150 or TRPV1 in vlPAG GABAergic neurons attenuated aversion, and AKAP150 knockdown reversed p-TRPV1 upregulation.
